Linh: Heads-up — since the kernel-selector change rolled last night we're seeing a spike in OOMs for AWQ / fp8 models on p3s, and p50 latency up ~18% on small-batch chat workloads. doing an initial triage.
Maya: Ugh. Any obvious alloc traces? is it KV cache dtype related or workspace sizing?
Linh: Profiling shows larger transient allocations during kernel handoff. The selector chooses a slightly different attention kernel that allocates a new temporary workspace per layer instead of reusing the long-lived workspace. Sample log excerpt:
```
alloc_workspace(layer=10, size=12.4MB) -> new
free_workspace(layer=10)
alloc_workspace(layer=11, size=13.1MB) -> new
// no reuse due to selector cached key mismatch
OOM when alloc_workspace(layer=17)
```
Raj: That matches the perf counters I grabbed — reuse_hits dropped from ~92% to ~63% across sequence lengths. Also noticed KV cache dtype casts are triggering ephemeral buffers: AWQ model tries to keep kv as fp8 but we upcast for some kernels, causing transient fp32 buffers.
Sofia: So two problems: (1) workspace reuse regression from kernel switching logic, (2) dtype upcast transient buffers increasing peak memory. Can we hotfix one at a time?
Linh: My plan: revert the kernel-selector heuristic that prefers the 'packed' attention on short sequences (quick rollback) and, in parallel, add a conservative soft-reserve bump for AWQ fp8 models to avoid immediate OOMs. Also propose a lightweight allocator change: prefer 'handoff' reuse — if a new kernel is chosen but a workspace with compatible size exists, hand it off instead of allocating.
Maya: How invasive is the handoff change? Could it introduce correctness issues if kernels expect different alignment/stride?
Linh: It's bounded: we add a compatibility predicate (dtype/buffer_alignment/size) before reuse. If incompatible, fall back to old behavior. Pseudocode:
```
if workspace_exists and is_compatible(workspace, kernel_req):
    assign(workspace)
else:
    alloc_new()
```
Should be safe.
Raj: For the kv dtype problem, suggest lazy upcast: don't create full fp32 shadow buffers up front. Instead allocate per-block when kernel needs it and free immediately. That reduces peak by ~20% based on our microbenchmarks.
Sofia: Can we also try a per-model config to force kv_storage_dtype=fp16 for AWQ until we have better fp8 kernels? It will trade accuracy slightly but may keep production stable.
Linh: Yep — we can ship a temporary model-config override via rollout rules in the control plane. Example rule for the short-term:
```
model: awq-7b-v2
routes:
  - match: "latency_sensitive"
    overrides:
      kv_storage_dtype: fp16
      soft_reserve_bytes: 64MB
```
Sofia: Nice. Who can do the rollback + allocator handoff PR?
Maya: I can handle the selector rollback (small toggle) and the rollout rule. Will open PR tonight.
Raj: I'll prototype the handoff predicate and the lazy-upcast change in a branch. Will post microbench numbers here when ready.
Linh: Good. For monitoring: add a short-lived alert on reuse_hit_rate < 80% and ephemeral_fp32_alloc_ratio > 0.15 so we can catch regressions during rollout.
infra-bot: deploybot: rollback toggle flagged for canary deploy on infra-canary-1.
Maya: After rollback, we should run the seq-latency job with AWQ chat trace and verify p50 back to baseline. Also run the oom-repro script (repro/oom-awq.sh) on p3-7b-spot.
Raj: repro results (local): handoff predicate reduced peak mem from 13.2GB -> 10.4GB on our AWQ trace, reuse_hit_rate back to 89%, p50 improved ~12%.
Linh: Awesome. Ok action items:
- Maya: rollback selector toggle + rollout rule (kv_storage_dtype fp16 + soft_reserve) — PR and canary today
- Raj: handoff predicate + lazy-upcast prototype + microbench numbers
- Linh: add monitoring alerts and update the incident runbook with steps to set model override
- Sofia: coordinate support and notify any customers in the canary pool
Maya: will also include a short note in #eng-runtime with the revert details.
Sofia: thanks everyone. if Raj's handoff looks stable we can keep it and remove the kv_storage_dtype override.
Linh: I'll keep the thread updated. If anyone catches an OOM during canary ping here + tag me. :thumbsup:
